newsitem.title: USA: Duff & Phelps upgrades Comcast debt.
newsitem.headline: Duff & Phelps upgrades Comcast debt.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co. said Tuesday it upgraded the ratings of Comcast Corp's senior subordinated debentures to double-B-plus from double-B and its convertible subordinated debentures to double-B from double-B-minus.
The upgrade affects about $1.8 billion of outstanding long-term debt.
The change reflects Comcast's improved financial flexibility resulting from Microsoft Corp's $1 billion equity investment, the rating agency said.

Comcast has the flexibility to use the cash investment to accelerate its network upgrade, including new product rollouts and debt reduction, share repurchases or other corporate uses, Duff & Phelps said.

This substantial cash position, along with expected credit improvements resulting from cash flow growth due in part to the integration of the Scripps cable acquisition into its core cable business, should give the company the ability to continue to produce financial results that are reflective of this rating category, it said.

The ratings also acknowledge the structural subordination resulting from the debt-service obligations of Comcast's subsidiaries and the potential financial variability of results in Comcast's electronic retailing and programming interests, Duff & Phelps said.

Duff & Phelps said it also reaffirmed the senior unsecured triple-B-minus rating of Comcast Cable Communications Inc. The rating could be reviewed if Comcast Corp uses some of this cash infusion to meaningfully affect financial levels or business risk at this entity.
